title: Tutorial: Put It All Together
scenario: This final tutorial step combines the ideas so far. Turn a list of environments into a map, then let a module consume that map with for_each so each environment gets its own stable instance.
constraints: Include var.project_name in each generated name.
The module uses local.environment_map with for_each.

focus.title: Build the module input map
focus.todo: Turn the environment list into a map of stable bucket names.

hints.why: This is the shape of a reusable environment pattern: a caller supplies a small list, a local derives stable keys, and a module creates one instance per key.
hints.what: Complete the environment_map local. Every environment should become a key whose value is a project-prefixed bucket name. The module call and output below are already wired.
hints.when: Use this composition when several environments need the same component and you want adding an environment to be a one-line change.
hints.how: Inside `locals`, add `environment_map` as a braced `for` expression over `var.environments`. Use the loop variable as both the map key and the environment name in the value, and build each value from `var.project_name` plus that name. The module call already consumes `local.environment_map`.

test_manifest.title: the environment map is built with a for expression
the map comprehension uses a key/value pair
the storage module uses the generated map
